modelAnswer:
When Mr. and Mrs. Green got home, Kevin went to talk to them. He told them about the man, the open window and the loose floorboard. “He said his parents used to live here and his father’s watch was hidden in the house,” Kevin added quietly. “We bought this house from an old couple years ago,” Mr. Green said slowly. “They did mention a son who worked far away.” Kevin led them inside and pointed to the board the man had tried to lift. Mr. Green fetched a screwdriver and pried it up. Underneath lay a small wooden box. Inside was an old silver watch.

Kevin and Mr. Green took the watch they had found to the police station. An officer listened to their story and checked the old house records. The man had told the truth: the house had belonged to his parents, and he had only come back for his father’s watch. Since nothing had been taken, Mr. Green decided not to press charges. When the man was brought out, Kevin stepped forward and handed him the box. “I’m sorry I chased you off,” he said. The man held the watch for a long moment. “You were right to stop me, kid. I should have knocked and asked.” Walking home beside Mr. Green, Kevin felt lighter. Finding out the truth had finally set his mind at rest.
